transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Soto (Celestia), Marcus Lee (Celestia), Priya Raman (Celestia)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, I'm Maya from Redwood, with Ravi our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Dr. Elena Soto: Hi Maya, hi Ravi. Thanks, we've got about an hour. High level: we want to scope a POC to validate open models for a biomedical assistant that will, uh, summarize clinical trial protocols and assist with regulatory Q&A.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Great, could you start with the success criteria - what would make the POC successful for you?
[00:40] Marcus Lee: Sure. The top three for us: one, quality - answers must be clinically accurate, low hallucination. Two, performance - P95 latency under 350 ms for single-turn summarization when possible. Three, security - no persistent logging of PHI and KMS-managed keys, SOC2 compliance. Also cost matters but it's secondary.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: Quick clarifying Q: when you say P95 350 ms, is that for inference on a dedicated node in your region, or for hosted?
[01:12] Dr. Elena Soto: Ideally for our Dedicated deployment in AWS eu-west-1. If hosted can't meet it then we need to see Dedicated numbers.
[01:20] Priya Raman: Also note we need multilingual support; English and Spanish primarily, a bit of French. And some domain adaptation for pharma terms.
[01:32] Maya Chen: Understood. For domain accuracy we'll propose a small eval set - about 200 prompts - and some human annotations to measure hallucination and factuality. We'll include a rubric.
[01:42] Marcus Lee: On workload: typical prompt length is about 450 tokens (we usually send a protocol excerpt + question), peak concurrency around 40-60 RPS for short bursts, average sustained 10-15 RPS.
[01:58] Ravi Patel: Good to know. For sizing that pushes us to consider model variants with batching and KV cache. We'll propose both a lower-latency config and a cost-optimized config.
[02:10] Dr. Elena Soto: What's your suggested model shortlist for an open-model POC? We want non-proprietary options and ability to run on our VPC.
[02:18] Maya Chen: Based on your needs - domain, multilingual, and latency - our initial shortlist is: Llama-2-chat-70B (quantized and server-optimized), Mistral-Instruct-22B (or 7B-instruct for faster), MPT-30B-instruct for structured outputs, and StarCoder/Code models only if you need code-like structured parsing. We'll also include Mixtral 8x7B variants for some balance.
[02:46] Priya Raman: Concern: larger models like 70B might give better quality but cost and latency could be prohibitive.
[02:52] Ravi Patel: Exactly - tradeoffs: Llama-2-chat-70B often has the best raw quality for instruction-following, especially on long context, but it needs more GPU RAM and higher per-token cost. Mistral-7B or 22B variants are usually strong on instruction and cheaper, and quantization can help but sometimes at a slight quality hit.
[03:10] Marcus Lee: We could accept a little quality drop if hallucination metrics remain low and latency is met. What's your metric for hallucinations?
[03:16] Maya Chen: We'll measure hallucination rate by comparing model outputs to gold annotations and flagging unsupported assertions; target less than 5% major hallucinations on the eval set. We'll also include a human-in-the-loop accept/reject sample.
[03:29] Dr. Elena Soto: Encryption - we need customer-managed KMS, full-disk encryption for on-prem, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that available?
[03:38] Ravi Patel: Yes. For Redwood Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations, audit log forwarding, RBAC and SSO/SAML. We'll send the SOC2/ISO docs. For Dedicated we can enable VPC peering and private endpoints.
[03:54] Maya Chen: For benchmarks, proposed plan: week 0 we exchange prompts and evaluation rubric, week 1 Redwood provisions nodes and runs baseline benchmarks with selected models, week 2 we run customer-supplied prompts and jointly review results. If results pass success criteria we move into a 6-week POC with data controls and more thorough integration testing.
[04:14] Marcus Lee: Sounds reasonable. For perf targets - besides P95 < 350 ms - also want sustainable throughput targets. For example, 20 RPS sustained with <1s median latency for our 450-token prompts.
[04:27] Ravi Patel: We'll include both latency and throughput targets in the spreadsheet. Also, caching: if you have repeated prefixes we can use prefix/KV caching to significantly reduce cost and latency - do you have repeating templates?
[04:38] Priya Raman: Yes quite a bit. The protocol summaries share common structure and headers. Caching could help.
[04:43] Maya Chen: We'll run two benchmark modes: cold (no cache) and warm (with prefix/KV caching) to show delta.
[04:52] Dr. Elena Soto: Ok. About evaluation - we need multilingual checks. Can Redwood run the same prompts across EN/ES/FR and show side-by-side metrics?
[04:59] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll run language parity tests. Note some models have weaker FR/ES performance; we'll flag that. For Spanish, Mistral and Llama family generally do well when fine-tuned or with instruction templates.
[05:12] Marcus Lee: How about hallucination mitigation - are there built-in tools?
[05:17] Maya Chen: We provide detection hooks and can run a secondary verification model, plus a retrieval-augmented pipeline for facts. For POC we can test both pure generation and RAG variants using your internal docs.
[05:29] Dr. Elena Soto: We absolutely need RAG for regulatory Q&A - can't risk hallucinating on guidance.
[05:34] Ravi Patel: We recommend RAG for any factual regulatory queries; for summarization you can often do constrained generation with templates. We'll demo a RAG setup in the perf run.
[05:43] Priya Raman: Timeline question - how long to provision dedicated infra?
[05:47] Ravi Patel: Typically 2\u20133 business days for a transient Dedicated node once we have access/permissions. If you want on-prem, that's longer and we'll need SRE coordination.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Quick note on cost: we'll include a cost estimator per 1M tokens for each model/config (quantized vs fp16), and projected monthly costs for your expected traffic.
[06:06] Marcus Lee: For budgeting we'll need a ballpark before committing; send both hosted and dedicated numbers.
[06:11] Maya Chen: Will do.
[06:14] [06:14] (speaker overlap, minor audio glitch)
[06:20] Dr. Elena Soto: For compliance - would Redwood's Dedicated instance be isolated so logs don't leave our account?
[06:26] Ravi Patel: Yes, we can configure log forwarding to your SIEM and ensure we don't persist PHI in our platform logs. For Private deployments you can run the entire control plane in your VPC.
[06:36] Marcus Lee: Any concerns about model licensing? Llama 2 is acceptable but we prefer models with permissive commercial terms.
[06:42] Maya Chen: We'll provide a licensing summary for each candidate model; Llama-2 commercial terms are OK with the right attribution, Mistral and others have varied terms - we'll document them.
[06:52] Priya Raman: On evaluation metrics - besides hallucination rate, we'd like ROUGE for summarization, and an accuracy metric for Q&A. Also human preference tests.
[06:59] Ravi Patel: We'll include automated metrics (ROUGE, BLEU where relevant), factuality checks, and a human eval plan.
[07:07] Dr. Elena Soto: For sample data we will anonymize PHI but preserve structure; is that ok?
[07:12] Maya Chen: Yes, anonymized samples are perfect for the initial bench. For on-prem tests we can run non-anonymized if you grant us the infra access.
[07:20] Marcus Lee: Communication - let's create a shared folder with the prompts, rubric, and any SSO details.
[07:25] Maya Chen: We'll set up a shared drive and upload the benchmark template.
[07:29] [07:29] Maya Chen: Recap of agreed items: Redwood to send benchmark template & cost model, provision transient Dedicated node, run cold/warm benchmarks across shortlisted open models (Llama-2-chat-70B quant, Mistral variants, MPT-30B, Mixtral), run multilingual checks and RAG variant, customer to provide 200 prompts and evaluation rubric.
[07:51] Dr. Elena Soto: Yep that matches. For the POC timeline after bench pass we'd aim for 6-week POC starting mid-April.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll aim to get the initial benchmark results back by 2026-03-29.
[08:05] Marcus Lee: One more thing: if a model fails on hallucination we want automatic fallback to a safer, smaller model rather than returning a confident wrong answer. Is that supported?
[08:15] Ravi Patel: Yes - Redwood routing policies can fallback at inference time to a conservative model variant or to a retrieval-only path. We'll configure that for you during POC.
[08:24] Priya Raman: Great. Any risks you foresee?
[08:27] Maya Chen: Main risks: data access/permissions delaying provisioning, domain-specific quality requiring more fine-tuning than expected, and unexpected licensing limits. We'll surface these early.
[08:38] Dr. Elena Soto: Ok thank you. We'll send the prompt set and rubric by 2026-03-24.
[08:45] Maya Chen: Thanks all - action items recap: Maya to send sheet and security docs; Ravi to provision infra; Elena to share prompts.
[08:52] Marcus Lee: Thanks, bye.
[08:54] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mis-heard acronyms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash) and a brief audio glitch around 06:14.
